title: Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


[USER].dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


[USER].fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

worked when ran with
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.57.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
stopped working at
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.58.0 streamlit run repro.py
```

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17011)

This is a regression from 1.57.0 to 1.58.0: a dialog opened from a button inside `[USER].fragment(run_every=...)` stays on screen after the parent fragment auto-reruns, but clicks inside it stop working and the backend logs `The fragment with id ... does not exist anymore`.

`[USER].dialog` is implemented as a nested fragment of the caller (`_fragment` wrapping the dialog body). Because the repro only calls `show_dialog()` on the button-click run, the parent `run_every` rerun never re-registers that nested fragment. Since 1.58.0 (PR #15130, the #15084 stale auto-rerun fix), `ScriptRunner` evicts descendants that were not re-registered via `clear_stale_descendants`. The frontend still shows the modal because dialogs live on `event_dg` (outside the parent fragment tree) and keep `isOpen` in React state. Later widget clicks send a fragment rerun for the evicted id; `AppSession.request_rerun` then drops the request at the `fragment_storage.contains` check. A likely fix is to keep an open dialog fragment across parent fragment reruns (or not treat dialogs as evictable descendants), rather than closing leftover UI.

### Related Issues

- [#15084](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15084) — Nested `run_every` fragments crashing when an ancestor stopped rendering them. The 1.58.0 descendant-eviction fix for this is the likely source of this regression; dialogs are nested fragments that are *intentionally* not re-called on later parent runs.
- [#16708](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16708) — Nested `run_every` fragment remains on screen with stale content after it is no longer rendered. Same leftover-UI class of bug (backend eviction vs. frontend still showing the subtree), though that report is about fragment containers rather than dialogs.
- [#10283](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10283) — `st.dialog` opened from a fragment has inconsistent dismiss/reopen behavior compared with a top-level dialog. Same feature intersection (dialog nested in a fragment) but a different lifecycle failure.
